Frontend (Subscription.jsx + AdminDashboard.jsx) correctly reads them from /subscription/status, so end-to-end behavior is unaffected — flagging as a spec deviation only.

action_items: OPTIONAL (spec-cosmetic, not a functional bug): Mirror downgraded_to_free_at + downgrade_reason on /api/auth/me to match the iter-47 spec exactly. No frontend depends on it today.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L7453: admin endpoint is named /remove-override but the iter-47 review request labels it /cancel-override. The actual code (and the AdminDashboard.jsx button at L1118) uses remove-override. Spec wording mismatch only — confirmed working as remove-override.

server.py L7396-7408: when admin assigns 'free' the helper sets downgraded_to_free_at=now() even for users who were never on a paid plan (e.g. assigning free to an already-free user). Causes the Subscription page downgrade-notice banner to render for that user. Minor UX nit, not a regression.

Free-plan card on landing page label reads '$0 /year' — the period '/year' is technically odd for a free-forever plan (mirrors Starter/Growth styling for visual consistency). Footnote 'Free forever — no credit card' clarifies it. Non-blocking copy nit.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter-47 fully verified. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration_47_free_plan.py is reusable as regression — uses pymongo (synchronous) to avoid motor's per-loop executor issue when running multiple sequential test cases that each spin a fresh event loop. To run the register-defaults-to-free test, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in /app/backend/.env must be blanked first and backend restarted; restore after. The 'cancel-override' wording in the iter-47 review request is a typo — the actual endpoint is /api/admin/users/{user_id}/remove-override. /auth/me does NOT include downgraded_to_free_at/downgrade_reason (spec deviation, non-functional); Subscription.jsx and AdminDashboard.jsx read them from /subscription/status which DOES include them. Frontend LiveDashboardDemo toast wording confirmed correct via source.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues. One minor spec deviation: /auth/me payload omits downgraded_to_free_at + downgrade_reason while /subscription/status includes them. Root cause: server.py get_me handler (L2437-2457) hard-codes a fixed response dict that was not updated when the two new persistence fields were added in iter-47. Mitigation: add `downgraded_to_free_at: user_doc.get('downgraded_to_free_at')` and `downgrade_reason: user_doc.get('downgrade_reason')` to the dict returned from get_me. Low priority — no UI is broken.
